Reproduce means to make something exist again — whether by creating new life, making a copy of something, recreating an experience or result, or playing back a sound or image. The word carries several distinct but closely related meanings, and understanding all of them will give you complete mastery of this word.

Every meaning of reproduce shares the same foundation: something that already exists is brought into existence again, in some form. A creature produces new creatures. A machine produces a copy of a document. A scientist makes an experiment happen again. A speaker plays back a sound. In each case, something is being re-made, re-created, or re-generated.

The most fundamental meaning of reproduce is when a living organism creates new individuals of its own kind. This applies to every living thing — animals, plants, fungi, bacteria, and viruses.

When rabbits have babies, they are reproducing. When a bacterium splits into two, it is reproducing. When a plant releases seeds that grow into new plants, it is reproducing. The word covers every possible mechanism — whether through sex, budding, splitting, spores, or cloning. It is a neutral, scientific term for the act of generating new life.

In this sense, reproduce is most often used without a direct object, meaning the subject simply does the action on its own. You say "Bacteria reproduce rapidly" rather than "Bacteria reproduce something." However, it can also be used with a reflexive pronoun or a direct object, for example: "The virus reproduces itself by hijacking healthy cells," or "These organisms can reproduce thousands of offspring in a single season."
Meaning 2 — To Make a Copy of Something

When you reproduce something — a document, an image, a piece of artwork, a piece of music — you make a copy or duplicate of it. This is very common in art, publishing, law, and everyday life.

Think of a photocopier: it takes an original document and reproduces it. A music app reproduces audio. A book publisher reproduces photographs inside a book. In each case, an original exists, and a version of it is being made again.

This meaning is always used with a direct object — reproduce always acts on the thing being copied. You reproduce the document, reproduce the painting, reproduce the image, reproduce the text.

An important nuance here: reproducing something does not always mean creating a perfect physical duplicate. It means making a version that closely represents the original. A photograph of a painting reproduces it, even though it is on paper and not canvas. A recording of a live concert reproduces the music, even though it is not identical to the live experience.

This sense also carries a strong legal dimension. Copying someone's original work without their permission can be a violation of copyright law, which is why you frequently see the phrase "not to be reproduced" stamped on official documents and copyrighted materials. When a publisher says "no part of this book may be reproduced," they mean you cannot copy it in any form without permission.
Meaning 3 — To Recreate or Replicate Something

This meaning is slightly more abstract, but equally important. When you reproduce a result, a condition, an effect, or a feeling, you make it happen again. You are not making a physical copy of a thing — you are re-creating an event, a situation, or an experience.

This sense is especially common in science. A fundamental rule of good science is that experiments must be reproducible — meaning anyone who follows the same steps, anywhere in the world, should arrive at the same results. If a scientist claims a discovery but no one else can reproduce the finding, it is considered unreliable and suspect.

The meaning extends well beyond science, though. You can try to reproduce an atmosphere, a mood, a feeling, or an artistic effect. For example: "He tried to reproduce the warmth of his grandmother's kitchen in his own home." "The director tried to reproduce the magic of the original film." "It is very hard to reproduce that kind of creative genius." In each case, someone is trying to make something that once existed — an experience, a feeling, a result — exist again.
Meaning 4 — (Of a Device) To Produce Sound or Image Accurately

In a more technical context, a device reproduces sound or images when it plays them back with accuracy. This is common in discussions of speakers, headphones, cameras, televisions, and screens.

For example: "These speakers reproduce sound with exceptional clarity." "The old camera did not reproduce colors accurately." "A good microphone should reproduce the human voice faithfully." Here, the subject is always the device or medium, and the object is the sensory output — sound, color, detail, image. The idea is that the device is faithfully re-creating something that was originally captured or recorded.
How Reproduce Differs from Similar Words

Reproduce vs. Copy — Both involve making a duplicate, but copy is more casual and everyday. Reproduce sounds more formal, scientific, or legal. You would say "copy this file" in casual speech, but "reproduce the original artwork" in a formal or professional context.

Reproduce vs. Replicate — These are very close in meaning when referring to experiments or results. Replicate is slightly more precise and scientific in tone; reproduce is broader and more widely used across different contexts. In a scientific setting, the two are often interchangeable.

Reproduce vs. Breed — Both relate to producing offspring, but breed is typically applied to domesticated animals and often implies that humans are involved in controlling the process. Reproduce is more neutral and scientific, applying naturally to any living organism, including humans, without that sense of human control.

In biology, you will see: reproduce sexually, reproduce asexually, reproduce rapidly, reproduce in large numbers, fail to reproduce, ability to reproduce.

In science and research, you will see: reproduce the results, reproduce the findings, reproduce the experiment, reproduce the conditions, impossible to reproduce, difficult to reproduce.

In art, media, and publishing, you will see: reproduce the image, reproduce the text, reproduce the artwork, right to reproduce, permission to reproduce, reproduced without authorization.

In audio and visual technology, you will see: reproduce sound, reproduce color, reproduce detail, reproduce faithfully, unable to reproduce accurately.

No matter which sense you encounter, ask yourself this one question: Is something being made to exist again? If the answer is yes, then reproduce is likely the right word. Whether it is a living organism making new life, a machine making a copy, a scientist re-running an experiment, or a speaker playing back music — the word always points to the same idea: something is being brought back into existence in one form or another.
